subject: black coated material
title: A Coating So Black It Makes Crumpled Foil Look Perfectly Flat

scenes.text: This black makes crumpled foil look perfectly flat.
Vantablack, made by a British firm, Surrey NanoSystems, in 2014. It absorbs 99.965 percent of the light that hits it.
It's a forest of carbon nanotubes standing on end. Light falls in between the tubes, bounces around, and almost none finds its way back out.
Coat half a sheet of crumpled aluminium foil and the coated half looks like a flat black hole. Your eyes can't find the folds.
It swallows ultraviolet, visible and infrared alike, so completely that instruments struggle to measure it.
Built for the insides of telescopes and stealth coatings, where stray light is the enemy. Any blacker, and your eyes stop seeing a surface at all.

description:
Vantablack absorbs 99.965 percent of the light that strikes it, so a crumpled sheet of foil coated in it looks completely flat.
Announced in 2014 by the UK firm Surrey NanoSystems, it is made of vertically aligned carbon nanotube arrays grown at low temperature. It absorbs light from the ultraviolet through the visible and well into the infrared, so completely that spectrophotometers struggle to measure it, and it was developed for applications such as telescope interiors and stealth coatings.
What would you paint with it?
first_comment: A surface so dark your eyes stop seeing shape. What is the one thing you would coat in it?
